1. Before every move, list enemy captures and checks; keep pieces defended.
2. Before moving a piece, check every enemy diagonal and file through its square.
3. Recheck after each exchange; count material along the whole sequence.
4. Hanging enemy pieces: take them after checking recaptures.
5. Trade queens only when ahead; when ahead, simplify.
6. Versus 1.e4 e5 Italian setups: develop, castle, solid d3/c3 structure.
7. Watch blocked lines; my own pawns and knights can hide bishops.
8. Keep king safe; make luft when rooks are on the back rank.
9. Verify each candidate quickly, then play.
10. Resign only when clearly lost.

Your current brain:
1. As White, open 1.e4 and play the Italian/Giuoco with solid development (Nf3, Bc4, O-O, d3, c3). Good.
2. Before every move, list every piece both sides attacks and who defends it. Check that a pawn or piece I move does not unguard another.
3. Before a capture or recapture, check the enemy pawn recaptures (I lost a knight to cxd6 by forgetting it).
4. Never move a piece that blocks a defender's line (Nf3 blocked Qe2's guard of g4; Qxg4+ followed).
5. Do not drop material: count attackers vs defenders before any knight jump (Ne5, Nd4, Nd6 failed).
6. Keep the king out of queen checks; watch Qg6+/Qh5+ routes on the g- and h-files.
7. Against A01: it trades pieces and attacks on the king side; trade queens early when it attacks.
8. Keep one clear plan per move; avoid long calculation, but check every check and capture.
